demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Triggers.value: Undergoing a medical examination or procedure

Maladaptive Strategies.value: keep mind occupied all the time

Threat.value: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience

Memory.value: The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it

Negative Appraisals.value: I can't trust that I will do the right thing
My life has been destroyed by the trauma
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within Memory, 'Feels Present Not Past' and 'Full Sensory Reliving' indicate highly intrusive, poorly contextualized trauma memory, which conflicts with 'Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.' These can sometimes coexist, but stated this strongly they pull in opposite directions and are hard to reconcile as the same memory profile.

issues.item: Threat: Watching Others: I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me
issues.explanation: The Threat items depict pervasive fear of being physically attacked by other people ('watch other people closely', 'back to wall', 'stay alert at night'), which does not fit well with the trauma type of accidentally causing serious injury to another. For this trauma, threat is more plausibly guilt, condemnation, or fear of consequences, not generalized interpersonal danger.

issues.item: Threat: Back to Wall: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room
issues.explanation: 'Mirror Checking' is not well linked to the rest of the profile. Nothing in Triggers, Memory, Threat, or Negative Appraisals suggests appearance-focused concern, dissociation needing visual reassurance, or checking for injury; as selected, it appears clinically disconnected.

Mirror checking is hard to reconcile with the trauma type of accidentally causing serious injury to another; it more strongly suggests concerns about visible injury, appearance, or being followed, none of which are supported by the other nodes.

issues.item: Back to Wall: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room
issues.explanation: Back-to-wall hypervigilance and scanning the room imply an interpersonal or attack-related threat context. That is difficult to integrate with the rest of the profile, which centers on guilt, reliving, and self-blame after accidentally injuring someone rather than danger from other people.

vignette: Rafael Hernandez still remembers the day he accidentally caused serious injury to a student during a school field trip. It's been over two years now, but the memory remains as vivid and visceral as if it happened yesterday. The sound of shattering glass, the smell of antiseptic wafting from the hospital corridors – these sensory details have become etched in his mind like a scar. As a school counselor, Rafael is no stranger to stress, but ever since that fateful day, he's found himself on edge whenever he encounters situations that remind him of the accident. Medical procedures, even routine ones, send his heart racing and make him want to flee. The smell of disinfectant, once a mundane odor, now transports him back to the hospital where the student was treated. Rafael has developed maladaptive strategies to cope with these triggers – he keeps his mind occupied all the time, whether it's by mentally rehearsing conversations or fidgeting with objects in his pocket. But these attempts at distraction only provide temporary relief. The memories of that day continue to haunt him, refusing to be relegated to the past. When they resurface, Rafael is overwhelmed by a sense of reliving the experience all over again – the sights, sounds, and smells combining to create an immersive and terrifying reality. He struggles to put words to what happened, as if the trauma has stolen his language. Rafael's negative appraisals have become a constant companion, whispering self-doubt and recrimination in his ear. "I can't trust that I will do the right thing," he tells himself. The event has convinced him that his life has been destroyed by the trauma, leaving behind only a trail of guilt and shame. He blames himself for what happened, replaying the incident over and over in an attempt to rewrite history. As Rafael navigates these treacherous waters, his maladaptive strategies become increasingly entrenched. Avoiding police officers or thinking about the event becomes second nature – he knows that confronting these reminders will only lead him down a rabbit hole of memories and emotions. He also starts to experience sleep vigilance, lying awake at night as if waiting for some new threat to emerge. Despite his best efforts, Rafael finds himself perpetually on edge, primed for physical reactivity whenever something triggers the memory of that day. His negative appraisals only intensify this state, creating a self-reinforcing cycle where memories and emotions feed into each other like a maelstrom. The event has warped his sense of time, leaving him feeling as if it's still happening – an ongoing catastrophe from which he cannot escape. It was the recent arrival of a new student at school that finally brought Rafael to seek help. As he watched the young boy nervously navigate the classroom, something inside him snapped. He knew he couldn't continue living like this – trapped in a cycle of avoidance and recrimination. For the first time since the accident, Rafael felt a glimmer of hope that maybe, just maybe, he could learn to live with his memories rather than be controlled by them. As he sits in his therapist's office, Rafael hesitantly begins to recount the events of that fateful day. The words come slowly at first, but as he speaks, something begins to shift inside him – a sense of release and possibility that has been eluding him for far too long.
